page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; a marginal note "Cap.6." stands in the right margin beside the line "genus ele-". Running head at the top with the printed page number 223.

main_text.p: tici[?] tentantur nullam inferri noxam tã uerum est,quàm quòd uerisimum. Igitur nō simpliciter,sed distinctione addita, dicitur contagiosa elephantiasis. Etenim tria tantùm habet tempora, ut cæteri exitiosi morbi,principium,incrementum & uigorem: in quò hic affectus ægrum haud dubiè è medio tollit.Itaq; si qua sit in hoc agresti & ferro morbo contages, illa profecto nó est in principio,nec in incremento,sed duntaxat in ipso uigore, quando uidelicet nó solùm naturalia uiscera,sed & pulmones, trachea arteria, fauces, palatum & nares admodũ putrefacta sunt, unde teter odor, flatus tũ expirat,quos posthac inspirant intusq; excipiunt, qui cùm huiusmodi elephanticis consuetudinem habent.Quæ autem tuberculosa est,uelut cancer occultus dicitur, ut & ulcerosa cancer ulceratus. Et quemad-modum hic ab atra bile adusta, ille uerò à succo melancholico originem ducit: ita e-lephantiasis, quæ extuberat à sanguine melancholico,& ulcerosa ab atra bile adassata[?] oritur.His addit Plinius libro,Naturalis historię,uicesimo quinto,tertium genus ele-Cap.6. phantiæ, quam albam appellat, cuius me-delam ibidem scribit esse ellebori albi radices.

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment, so it is marked cont="true". "tici" is doubtful at the top left. "adassata" is doubtful; the printed word may read "adassata" or "adaffata". "teter" is printed as "tetet" in the scan and is kept as the printed form in spelling where the context suggests "teter". The word "radices" is split across two lines ("radi" / "ces.") without a printed hyphen, so it is joined.
